title: Scanopy daemon first-initialization boundary may be LAN-reachable with host-level privileges
description: The repository gives scanopy-daemon host networking, privileged container mode and the raw Docker socket. Current Scanopy upstream defaults the daemon listener to 0.0.0.0:60073 and exposes /api/initialize without authentication before the once-only initialization guard is satisfied. Because this repository deploys the unpinned :latest image and this audit did not inspect the live daemon state or firewall, exploitability of the deployed instance is not established.
claimed_root_cause: A high-privilege daemon is attached directly to the host network and Docker socket without a target-side bind restriction or immutable image reference; whether its pre-initialization public API is reachable depends on the deployed upstream version and host/network controls.

trace.description: network_mode: host places the daemon listener directly on host networking.
privileged: true grants broad host-facing container capabilities.
The raw Docker socket is mounted into the daemon; :ro on a Unix socket mount does not itself create a read-only Docker API.

evidence.description: Daemon receives the raw Docker socket.

blockers: The target image is ghcr.io/scanopy/scanopy/daemon:latest, so the exact deployed source revision is not pinned.
The live daemon initialization state and effective bind/listen address were not inspected.
TrueNAS/pfSense host-firewall reachability of TCP/60073 was not inspected.
The audit execution policy forbids active probes against the shared/live homelab.

validation_plan.local: On an isolated throwaway host, run the exact deployed image digest with dummy state and no real Docker socket, then verify whether a first initialization request is accepted without authentication and whether sensitive initialization material is written to logs.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed only: record docker image digest, passively inspect the listener with ss/sockstat, verify firewall policy for TCP/60073, and check whether the daemon config is already initialized without printing network IDs/API keys. Do not send a synthetic initialization request to the live daemon.
